newsitem.title: CANADA: Saputo doesn't rule out higher Ault bid.
newsitem.headline: Saputo doesn't rule out higher Ault bid.

text.p: Saputo Group Inc said on Monday it did not rule out a higher offer for Ault Foods Ltd but needed details of a white knight bid by Parmalat Finanziaria SpA and access to Ault's books.
Parmalat, Italy's largest publicly traded food company, today bid C$34 a share cash for Ault, topping privately held, Montreal-based Saputo Group's C$28 a share all-cash offer in May.
Ault's board endorsed the Parmalat offer.
Saputo executive vice-president Camillo Lisio told Reuters that Saputo needed access to Ault's books before considering a higher bid.
"It's possible only if we have access to the books," Lisio said in a telephone interview. "We certainly don't have the privilege of knowing what Parmalat knows about the company."
Ault Chief Executive Graham Freeman said another offer would have to top C$35 a share, considering a breakup fee of C$1 a share included in the Parmalat deal.
Lisio added: "The only thing I know is that we have the money and we can do a transaction. Otherwise we would not have gotten involved in this game."

Freeman said in a telephone interview that Saputo did not qualify for access to Ault's books because it had not agreed to a confidentaility agreement, unlike Parmalat and other unidentified, interested parties.
Freeman also noted that Lisio said originally he could raise or lower Saputo's C$28 bid after looking at the books, which Freeman said could have hurt shareholder value.
Saputo owns 16.3 percent of Ault, Lisio said.

Lisio added that Saputo was intent on becoming a worldwide player in the dairy field. "Our efforts are still concentrated on Ault Foods and we still believe that something could be done, to the degree that we're given the ability to assess the real value of this company is," Lisio said.

Toronto-based Ault produces cheese, butter and other products through its 10 plants and 1,994 employees. Saputo is also a leading dairy foods maker along with its real estate and transportation interests.
Ault has a 14 percent share of the Canadian national market in cheese and margarine, 36 percent in butter and 26 percent of the liquid milk market in Quebec.
((Lydia Zajc, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8109 or lydia.zajc@reuters.com))
